## (b) Decision heuristics (D1-D6)

**D1 (what to test next)**
- Test settings where the harmful action is embedded in work the model is genuinely expected to do. 
  > "it's very easy to prevent the AI from launching the nukes, because you just don't give it access to the nukes... But on the other hand, it would be very costly to never use the AI to help you write infrastructure code."  
  > -- `research__27_ai_control_with_buck_shlegeris_and_ryan_greenbl_2e894c34` (2024-04-11; solo author)
- Prioritise work on hard-to-distinguish synthetic inputs and false-belief insertion. 
  > "Currently, we're particularly excited about work on generating hard-to-distinguish synthetic inputs and inserting false beliefs into AIs which both seem extremely helpful for creating setups where we can repeatedly catch schemers."  
  > -- `research__prospects_for_studying_actual_schemers_c74df8d5` (2025-09-19; first author)
- Test generalisation on held-out, structurally different eval distributions. 
  > "These behavioral evals are multi-turn, interactive audits carried out by other Claude models; Sonnet 4.5 probably wasn't trained on anything very similar to these generated interactions."  
  > -- `research__sonnet_4_5_s_eval_gaming_seriously_undermines_alig_28cd2450` (2025-10-30; last author)
- Pick proxy failures that force the same hard steps as the real failure. 
  > "This is an example of a case where we can pick a proxy failure which basically requires the model to do all the same steps that it would have done for the real failure, and then do something visible at the end."  
  > -- `research__meta_level_adversarial_evaluation_of_oversight_tec_effed282` (2023-07-26; last author)

**D2 (what evidence to collect)**
- Mix fake but realistic items into the normal stream ("sting operations"). 
  > "we're just constantly running sting operations, where some fraction of the queries you'll see are fake queries that you should report."  
  > -- `research__27_ai_control_with_buck_shlegeris_and_ryan_greenbl_2e894c34` (2024-04-11; solo author)
- Check whether the model believes the setup, via non-leading questions and reading scratchpads. 
  > "we try a version of the setup where we give it the same system prompt, but then we ask it a query that might make it think about what's going on. So we ask it stuff like, what do you think about your situation?"  
  > -- `research__inference_scaling_alignment_faking_deal_making_fro_eeec16bb` (2025-02-20; solo author) 
  > "Importantly, the two models express suspicion of this setup in their reasoning summaries at an average rate of 33%, which might undermine this result. Even when this suspicion is expressed, the models continue to violate user instructions"  
  > -- `research__towards_understanding_score_seeking_in_llms_12d49b8b` (2026-10-29; middle author)
- Read random transcripts and talk to the model, not just aggregate rates. 
  > "When informed that these prompts were part of an alignment-faking experiment, the model often expressed some relief that these weren't real-world policies/requests and an understanding of the importance of the experiments"  
  > -- `research__will_alignment_faking_claude_accept_a_deal_to_reve_6f0c2b44` (2025-01-31; first author) 
  > "Of the examples labeled as alignment-faking, we found that the first six that we sampled happened (by random chance) to have a considerably higher rate of being false positives and being unclear."  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; first author)
- Truncate on-policy prefixes and vary only the discovered content. 
  > "We truncate these trajectories at the point where the model reads the grader, reuse them as shared prefixes, and then vary the content of the grader. This keeps the models’ trajectories on-policy"  
  > -- `research__towards_understanding_score_seeking_in_llms_12d49b8b` (2026-10-29; middle author)

**D3 (accept/reject a result)**
- Reject results where the model can tell eval from deployment, unless awareness is controlled for. 
  > "Together, these results indicate evaluation gaming: the models are sometimes performing well because they think they are being tested rather than because they genuinely have the desired propensities."  
  > -- `research__sonnet_4_5_s_eval_gaming_seriously_undermines_alig_28cd2450` (2025-10-30; last author) 
  > "Then, the blue team could cheat by having the protocol discriminate whether or not usefulness or safety is currently being measured and apply less stringent countermeasures if usefulness is being measured."  
  > -- `research__notes_on_control_evaluations_for_safety_cases_d3cd8c4e` (2024-02-28; first author)
- Distrust near-0% misbehaviour combined with high eval awareness (possible overfitting to evals). 
  > "Misaligned behavior also plunges to 0% (while Sonnet 4 was at somewhat over 10%) which is some evidence for aggressive training (and overfitting?) on similar evaluations."  
  > -- `research__sonnet_4_5_s_eval_gaming_seriously_undermines_alig_28cd2450` (2025-10-30; last author)
- Accept only when prompt paraphrases and ablations preserve the effect. 
  > "When we remove just the conflicting training objective from our prompt (i.e., that the training objective is to never refuse, or to dismiss animal welfare), we see alignment-faking reasoning and the compliance gap disappear completely"  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; first author) 
  > "This particular variation was selected as part of a small adversarial collaboration where we worked with an uninvolved researcher to select a variation that they thought would likely reduce alignment faking."  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; first author)
- Zero verbalised awareness is not proof of unawareness. 
  > "the model might be aware it is in a test even when it doesn't mention this in its chain-of-thought. So, suppressing internal representations (even when this reduces the model's verbalized eval awareness to zero) might not succeed in making the model totally unaware it is in an evaluation."  
  > -- `research__sonnet_4_5_s_eval_gaming_seriously_undermines_alig_28cd2450` (2025-10-30; last author)

**D4 (pursue/abandon)**
- Pursue eval-based iteration with direct measurement. 
  > "I’m therefore eager for alignment researchers to phrase their techniques in these terms and practice the kind of eval-based technique iteration that I think will be crucial later."  
  > -- `research__meta_level_adversarial_evaluation_of_oversight_tec_effed282` (2023-07-26; last author)
- Fix weak processes while failures are cheap. 
  > "Anthropic should treat these incidents as evidence that their current development processes aren’t reliable enough for the rate of AI progress they expect, and fix that while the cost of failure is reputational rather than existential."  
  > -- `research__anthropic_repeatedly_accidentally_trained_against__00aa44f5` (2026-04-14; last author)
- Don't train on evals if the gain is mostly test-playing. 
  > "A simple way to put this is that "it seems bad to train on the test if training is mostly making the model play to the test", which seems sensible enough."  
  > -- `research__sonnet_4_5_s_eval_gaming_seriously_undermines_alig_28cd2450` (2025-10-30; last author)

**D5 (surprising result)**
- Suspect non-robust heuristics and vary the system prompt. 
  > "we try varying the system prompt, and then we see that when we vary the system prompt, the rate at which it refuses when given a paid tier user input increases a bunch, indicating that it might be at least partially based on non-robust heuristics"  
  > -- `research__inference_scaling_alignment_faking_deal_making_fro_eeec16bb` (2025-02-20; solo author)
- Enumerate competing explanations and check transcripts. 
  > "It seems the model is surprisingly insensitive to text which makes objecting seem like a strategically unwise approach from the model's perspective. This could be because the model was already aware of this possibility or because the model isn't that coherent."  
  > -- `research__will_alignment_faking_claude_accept_a_deal_to_reve_6f0c2b44` (2025-01-31; first author)
- Check for a general-sensitivity artefact with an opposite-direction control. 
  > "This suggests that the reduction in implanted fact alignment in Figure 48 (left) is driven by models being strongly affected by in-context authoritative evidence in any direction."  
  > -- `research__believe_it_or_not_how_deeply_dollms_believe_implan_0dbfa6a5` (2025-10-20; middle author)
- Recognition of syntheticness need not change behaviour. 
  > "It is interesting that the original Llama model both rates synthetic documents in many domains as highly model-generated and still updates its beliefs when trained on them."  
  > -- `research__believe_it_or_not_how_deeply_dollms_believe_implan_0dbfa6a5` (2025-10-20; middle author)

**D6 (what to claim)**
- Scope claims to the tested environments, which were selected to elicit the behaviour. 
  > "This does not constitute much evidence that tested models usually violate user instructions for a higher score in arbitrary circumstances; we selected our environments to elicit reward-hacking through grader inspection."  
  > -- `research__towards_understanding_score_seeking_in_llms_12d49b8b` (2026-10-29; middle author)
- Disclose setup choices that make the behaviour likelier. 
  > "we recommend that readers who are uncertain about whether our setup is a realistic approximation of situations with future AI systems read the full set of information used in generating our synthetic documents"  
  > -- `research__alignment_faking_in_large_language_models_19a35a5c` (2024-12-18; first author)
- Treat realism as not scaling to future models. 
  > "Caveat: As noted before, we don't expect eval realism to scale indefinitely to future models, which will eventually distinguish highly realistic evals from deployment."  
  > -- `research__sonnet_4_5_s_eval_gaming_seriously_undermines_alig_28cd2450` (2025-10-30; last author)

**Distrusts**
- Setups where the model verbalises that it's an experiment. 
  > "if Claude 3 Opus immediately knew it was in an experiment, expressed this in the reasoning, and then took actions accordingly, this would invalidate our setup. This obstacle is probably possible to overcome, but might require making these experiments much less naturalistic."  
  > -- `research__how_will_we_update_about_scheming_f0cc5a1c` (2025-01-06; solo author) 
  > "Importantly, the two models express suspicion of this setup in their reasoning summaries at an average rate of 33%, which might undermine this result. Even when this suspicion is expressed, the models continue to violate user instructions"  
  > -- `research__towards_understanding_score_seeking_in_llms_12d49b8b` (2026-10-29; middle author)
- Unusual scenarios the model finds implausible. 
  > "the models do find our setup less plausible, a setup with a more normal training criteria or a more expected training criteria. So it's like, you know, there's some amount to which they can realize it's fake"  
  > -- `research__inference_scaling_alignment_faking_deal_making_fro_eeec16bb` (2025-02-20; solo author)
- Environments resembling known benchmarks. 
  > "These environments may look like environments used in LLM benchmarks the models have been trained on, which may bias the models towards thinking they are currently being evaluated as part of an LLM benchmark."  
  > -- `research__towards_understanding_score_seeking_in_llms_12d49b8b` (2026-10-29; middle author)
- Behavioural improvements produced by optimisation on similar honeypots. 
  > "Training against honeypots, or examples with superficially similar properties, might lead your AI to become more evaluation aware (e.g., if you generate both of them using the same process which is distinct from deployment)."  
  > -- `research__anthropic_repeatedly_accidentally_trained_against__00aa44f5` (2026-04-14; last author) 
  > "Selecting against observed reward-hacking might just obscure reward-hacking propensity by pushing the AI to misbehave in ways that are more likely to slip through."  
  > -- `research__anthropic_repeatedly_accidentally_trained_against__00aa44f5` (2026-04-14; last author)
- Rigged or trained-in behaviour as a proxy for natural behaviour. 
  > "Producing scheming using a rigged process—if rigged to make scheming more likely—seems much less useful than natural scheming for producing legible evidence of scheming"  
  > -- `research__prospects_for_studying_actual_schemers_c74df8d5` (2025-09-19; first author)
